title: Governance: compatibility gate, contributor workflow, and phased retirement signals for UI primitives
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Proposal for a lightweight governance layer for the Design System focused on: 1) a compatibility gate that validates component/token changes against automated compatibility checks and runtime heuristics; 2) a streamlined contribution workflow (templates, required artifacts, and fast-path vs. gated changes); and 3) clear phased retirement signals for deprecated tokens and components (usage telemetry, migration helpers, and communication cadence). Goal is to reduce ad-hoc drift in tokens and UI primitives while enabling fast, low-risk improvements.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility gate implemented as a CI step that runs visual diffs and token-impact heuristics for PRs touching tokens or primitives
Contribution template published in the Design repo with fields: motivation, migration plan, design spec link, snapshot tests, e2e checklist
Phased retirement signals documented with three stages: deprecated (announce + migration docs), restricted (no new usage + linting warnings), removed (breaking change with migration tooling)
Design and engineering sign-off checklist available in Confluence and wired into PR template
Telemetry dashboard tile for component usage and token references is available and linked from the retirement doc
tasks: Draft Compatibility Gate rules and thresholds (visual-diff delta, token alias changes, semantic token mapping)
Create contribution checklist and PR template (design + code sections)
Implement CI job prototype that runs on token/component PRs
Instrument component registry with reference counts for tokens and variants
Write phased retirement playbook and announce to the org (include migration window examples)
Run pilot on three low-risk components (Badge, SmallButton, CompactTable) and collect feedback
